question: Will Haiti hold the first round of its presidential election before December 14, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Haiti's CEP on Oct 6, 2026 postponed the electoral campaign, extended candidate registration to Oct 31, and a CEP member said 'the December 13 date no longer stands'; outlets reported the elections postponed indefinitely with no new date. With registration open until Oct 31, no campaign dates, and no published calendar, holding a first-round presidential vote by Dec 13 is logistically implausible. Haiti's base rate of slipping announced election dates is very high (e.g., Aug 30, 2026 date already slipped to Dec 13). Residual mass covers a surprise reinstatement. No human prediction market found on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold.
calls.dossier:
- Jul 28, 2026 (Haitian Times / Caribbean National Weekly): CEP set first round of presidential+legislative elections for Dec 13, 2026, runoff Feb 21, 2027; CEP conditioned dates on acceptable security climate and funding.
- Nov 2025 (Haitian Times): earlier tentative first-round date was Aug 30, 2026 — later slipped to Dec 13.
- Oct 5, 2026: electoral decree modified (financial requirements for candidates eased) after consultations with political actors (Miami Herald, Oct 12).
- Oct 6, 2026 (Haitian Times, HPN, Rezo Nodwes): CEP extended online candidate registration to Oct 31, 2026, postponed the official campaign period; new dates to come with an updated calendar 'as soon as possible'. As of Oct 6: 12 presidential candidates registered.
- Oct 7, 2026 (France24, Breitbart, Outre-mer La 1ere): reported as indefinite postponement; a CEP member quoted: 'the December 13 date no longer stands... we are working on a new timetable.'
- Oct 12, 2026 (La Repubblica): UN rights chief cites at least 5,800 killed/injured by gang violence in 2026; ~300 armed groups, 70-75% in Port-au-Prince.
- Oct 12, 2026 (Miami Herald): date 'expected to be postponed'; UN briefing by SRSG Ruiz Massieu scheduled Oct 22.
- Sep 3, 2026 (NYT): experts said violence likely to force postponement.
- Status quo: no presidential vote held in Haiti since 2016; no current official date for first round.
- Base rate note: Haiti's announced election dates have repeatedly slipped (2015-16 annulled/re-run cycle, 2019 and 2021-2025 dates never held, Aug 30, 2026 date moved). Cases where the CEP itself suspended the date within ~10 weeks of polling and the vote nonetheless occurred on schedule: none found.
- Resolution: resolves off official popular voting beginning for the presidential election before Dec 14, 2026; Senate/Chamber-only votes do not count.
- Event window: now (Oct 14, 2026) -> Dec 14, 2026; window opened with question; roughly 0% of the remaining voting opportunity has passed — first round had been set for Dec 13.
- Searched, absent: any newly published CEP calendar after Oct 7, 2026; any Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market on this event.
calls.reference_class: Announced Haitian election dates since 2015 that were officially suspended by the CEP less than ~10 weeks before polling day

calls.reasoning: On Oct 6, 2026 the CEP postponed the campaign, which was due to start Oct 5, and extended candidate registration to Oct 31. It promised a revised calendar, and a CEP member said 'the December 13 date no longer stands'; media describe the delay as indefinite or sine die. Haiti has postponed its post-2016 electoral calendars many times and faces severe gang violence. Even if registration closes on Oct 31, a campaign plus logistics before Dec 13 is implausible. The press reports speculation that voting slips to 2027. No human prediction market was found (Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi). Small residual chance: the CEP reinstates a compressed December date.

A CEP member told AFP that 'the December 13 date no longer stands'. Haiti has repeatedly missed electoral target dates (Nov 2025, Aug 30 2026) and hasn't held a national election since 2016. Gang violence is extreme. Six weeks between registration closing and Dec 13 is not enough to run a campaign and a vote. calls.reconciliation: All three runs cite the same evidence: the Oct 5-6 CEP adjustment (registration extended to Oct 31, campaign postponed), the Oct 7 AFP quote that Dec 13 'no longer stands', the Oct 12 Miami Herald report that a postponement is expected, and the history of repeated slippage. No factual claims conflict, and the runs differ in no judgment that matters. I had no web access on this run, so I retrieved nothing new. Because the date was withdrawn by the CEP itself, not just put at risk, and the logistics window is now infeasible, I go slightly below the runs' 2%.
